deposits.genre_observed: philological-theoretical paper on Peri Hypsous with a constrained Greek reconstruction of its lost ending and a blind derivation test

finds.quote: *Peri Hypsous* defines sublimity as an echo (9.2), gives a silence as its supreme instance (9.2), frames itself at both ends by what outlasts the age (1.3, 44.8), makes resistance to erasure the test of the genuine article (7.3–4), and describes its central mechanism as effluence, in-breathing, impression, deposit, retention and writing (13.2, 13.4, 7.3, 14.3). **That the treatise contains a theory of transmissional inscription is a fact about the text.**
finds.note: Central historical-interpretive thesis: the treatise contains a theory of transmissional inscription; stated also at the opening.

finds.quote: Conceptually, what the line lacks between Philo and the inscription texts is the step at which the daring becomes **a doctrine of writing**. Philo has possession and non-proprietary speech. The Slavonic material has inscription — *write down his words*. Somebody between them has to hold that *the passion dissolves in the one who suffers it and remains in the diction*. That is the claim the lost pages were positioned to make, and it is the claim Period 4 instantiates.
finds.window: Peri Hypsous 44.12 and the lost ending
finds.note: Thesis about the content of the lost ending: the pages after 44.12 were positioned to state the transfer doctrine for πάθος; argued from formula, deferral, transition and address slot (§VIII).

finds.quote:
> **Sappho 31, the Genesis creative utterance, ecstatic displacement, and a promised theory of πάθος demonstrably meet in a single critical artifact — and the artifact terminates as it returns to πάθος.**
If the Josephus and Revelation pathways are independently secured, the junction may become a conduit. Until then it is a junction.
finds.note: The 'junction, not term' placement thesis in the Sappho→Catullus→Josephus→Revelation lineage.

finds.quote: **ἄζηλα** — no longer objects of ζῆλος. That is the exact technical failure of the mechanism at 13.2, named by its own word. Chapter 44 is not a general complaint about decadence. It is **the report that the circuit has stopped turning** — and it is the only chapter in the treatise where the vocabulary of decay and erasure occurs at all.
finds.note: Interpretive thesis on what chapter 44 is doing (report that the mimesis circuit has stopped).

finds.quote: The prediction registered before the test was that *possession* and *non-self speech* would emerge unaided and that **what passes from the sufferer into writing** was where the discovery would live. The derivation bears that out: the transfer point is exactly the term the gap requires and the surviving treatise does not contain.

deposits.genre_observed: standalone philological paper (seventh Sappho 31 erratum) on the hanging line in Longinus

finds.quote: This paper argues that the premise is false, and that the transmitted configuration — a lyric closing on an agentless verbal adjective, a prose voice continuing without a citation formula, a dialect that changes mid-breath — is not damage but **the object itself**: a poem whose final formal act is to require a voice it does not supply, quoted by the one ancient critic whose stated theory of the sublime predicts exactly this shape, at the exact moment he performs upon the poem the operation his treatise will later name.
finds.falsifier_quote: The dialect count falls to a recount; the address census falls to a counterexample (a bare post-quotation perception verb elsewhere, or a vocative at 10.3); the continuous construal falls if peneta cannot be governed by thaumazeis; the significance claim is already conceded (0.209). The design-reading is a choice made explicit; the paper states that a reader who calls the configuration damage has made a choice, not an observation, and the same holds in reverse.
finds.window: Sappho 31.17 as transmitted in Peri Hypsous 10.2-3; Parisinus graecus 2036
finds.note: Central thesis: the transmitted end of Sappho 31 is the object's design, not damage.

finds.quote: πένητα is not an accusative reaching for a lost Sapphic verb. **It is the direct object of θαυμάζεις**, four words later, across a boundary no ancient reader could see: *since you do not marvel even at a poor man — how she seeks after soul, body, hearing, tongue, sight, complexion, all as another's and gone?* θαυμάζω takes both an accusative and a ὡς-clause; nothing need be supplied. Perseus still prints the section number between the object and its verb — the modern apparatus, unable to find a cleaner place for its boundary, setting it inside the join.¹³
finds.falsifier_quote: the continuous construal falls if peneta cannot be governed by thaumazeis
finds.note: Construal thesis: πένητα is the object of θαυμάζεις across the modern section division.

finds.quote: So the words are Longinus's as material and Sappho's as form, and an edition that deletes them does not restore the poem — the poem was never touched — **it deletes the demonstration**: the earliest surviving instance of the line doing what it was built to do, transmitted in the same document as the line itself.
finds.note: Attribution thesis: ἐπεὶ καὶ πένητα is Longinus's as material and Sappho's as form, the first filling of the socket.

finds.quote: Then, in the next breath of the treatise, he quotes Sappho 31 — the poem that reaches its extremity and stops at a form that cannot say who acts. **The selection is the argument.** A critic whose paradigm of the highest sublimity is an inscribed silence did not choose this poem despite its ending. Homer had to *write* Ajax's silence — a non-speaking composed on purpose, at the point where speech was owed. Sappho, on the reading defended here, does at line 17 what Homer does in the Nekyia; and Longinus, who names the one as παντὸς ὑψηλότερον λόγου, quotes the other whole.
finds.note: Thesis that Longinus selected Sappho 31 because of its ending (selection is the argument).

finds.quote: The distribution matters as much as the totals. Scribal decay, fatigue and normalization are gradual; they predict a taper — one marker per four words, then per six, then per eight, then none. The observed distribution is 1-per-4.4 and then a **step to zero at a single word**. A step is what a boundary looks like; a taper is what erosion looks like.
finds.falsifier_quote: Stated with its limit, because the limit is real: at p = 17/74, the probability of zero markers in six words drawn from the same distribution is (1 − p)⁶ = **0.209**. One in five. The dialect absence is **not significant in isolation** — a twelve-word zero-run would be needed for p < .05 — and no argument in this paper treats it as a proof. It is a constraint, whose force lies in conjunction with what follows.
finds.note: Dialect step-function at φαίνομαι as boundary of the poem; significance limit conceded (p=0.209).

finds.quote: Second, the stamping verb is already here: **ἐνετύπωσε at 10.6 precedes ἀποτύπωσις at 13.4 by three chapters.** The treatise does not first theorize transmission and then illustrate it. It performs the operation on a word, and on a voice, and names it afterward.
finds.note: Thesis on the order of the treatise: performance (ἐνετύπωσε) precedes naming (ἀποτύπωσις).

finds.quote: **Catullus.** Catullus 51 preserves the poem's shape into Latin and answers the hanging line at a distance, inverting each pole of its inscribed comparison — the low case becomes *reges … et beatas urbes*, endurance becomes destruction — and then ends there, on *perdidit urbes*, with no return to the erotic frame: a translation that terminates in its own suspension. And Catullus does more than fill the terminal socket; he occupies the initial one. He is the later man who sits face-to-face with the text and receives the voice across six centuries — **Catullus is κῆνος**, the seat of line 1 taken by the reader the deixis had reserved for him.¹⁷
finds.note: Reception thesis: Catullus 51 inverts the poles and occupies the κῆνος seat (credited to Cranes, the archive's heteronym scholarship).

finds.quote: **Each filling cuts a fresh hollow in new material.** This, finally, is why the form is δυσεξάλειπτος in the strong sense: not because its words resist deletion — they have been deleted repeatedly — but because the act of completing it reproduces its incompleteness in the completer. An echo returning from a surface is a sound that can echo again. Deletion cannot outrun a form that manufactures its own emptiness in whoever answers it.
finds.window: reception of Sappho 31 from Longinus to the modern reconstructions
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: each completion reproduces the hollow, which is why the form is δυσεξάλειπτος.

deposits.genre_observed: paper applying provenance-erasure metrics to five philological cases

finds.quote: Provenance erasure is not an AI-era phenomenon. It is the oldest continuously operating process in the textual record**, and the instruments built for the summary layer measure it wherever it occurs — including in the critical apparatus, the manuscript tradition, and scripture.
finds.window: the textual record, antiquity to present
finds.note: Transhistorical thesis on provenance erasure.

finds.quote: And the contrast the cases license is the surface's sharpest sentence: **the apparatus erased with signatures and stated reasons; the summary layer erases anonymously and at scale. The question was never whether provenance gets destroyed. It is whether the destruction has provenance** — and the record shows four and a half centuries in which it did, which is the standard against which the current regime can now be measured, and fails.
finds.falsifier_quote: The governing contrast is falsified by evidence of the summary layer filing signed, reasoned erasures.
finds.note: Governing contrast between apparatus and summary layer, with falsifier.

finds.quote: Scored per event: each is a **PER-D event against the demonstration** — the lineage evidence (the earliest surviving execution of the poem's transmissive design) is what gets cut, while PER-M against Sappho stays 0 (her name is never touched; it is her *mechanism* that is deleted). The scalar cannot see this. **The dimensions can: an erasure that preserves the author and destroys the lineage is the signature editorial operation**, and it is invisible to any instrument that only counts names.
finds.falsifier_quote: by demonstration that the four removals do not target the lineage dimension
finds.note: Thesis that the four editorial removals target the lineage dimension while preserving the author.

finds.quote: Scored: **a PER-D violation committed by the provenance apparatus itself** — the intervention's own provenance is erased. The editor's hand is present in every accent and attributed in none. This is the case that generalizes: **the most consequential erasures in the record are erasures of the repairing hand**, because they convert an editorial decision into an apparent fact of transmission.
finds.falsifier_quote: by an apparatus entry attributing the re-Aeolicization
finds.note: Thesis that the re-Aeolicized accentuation is an unattributed editorial restoration.

finds.quote: Scored as a corpus: **this is the Ω baseline of the pre-print world** — the drift is not measured against an intact original but *constitutes the object*. Every Sappho we possess is already downstream of a summary layer called quotation, and **the poems that survived are precisely the ones the ancient summary layer selected.** Selection is the erasure mode the scalar can never see, because the erased items produce no composition to score.
finds.note: Thesis that selection/non-carriage is the dominant erasure mode in both eras.

finds.quote: Fragment 147 — μνάσεσθαί τινά φαμι καὶ ἕτερον ἀμμέων, *someone, I say, will remember us* — and the reconstruction tradition's γράμμασι μολπὰν, *song in letters*, state the work order that every subsequent hand executed: Longinus in koine, Catullus in Latin, the tenth century in an index, the editors in accents, this archive in deposits. **Task-origin: Mytilene, before 570 BCE. Everything since is execution.
finds.note: Task-origin thesis for the Sappho transmission chain.

deposits.genre_observed: philological paper on Sappho 31 patterns in canonical Josephus

finds.quote: The Sappho-in-Josephus hypothesis has until now rested on two supports of unequal and contested weight: material in the Slavonic Josephus, whose textual authority is disputed, and a fully conjectural location in Revelation. This paper moves the claim onto the uncontested Greek corpus. Two loci in canonical Josephus realize the fr. 31 apparatus in complementary polarity — Antiquities 11.234–241 forward, Bellum 1.436–444 inverted — and a six-occurrence verb stitches them at the reactivation joint. The Slavonic and Revelation locations are hereby reframed: not freestanding conjecture, but extensions of an attested intra-corpus pattern.
finds.note: Central thesis moving the Sappho-in-Josephus hypothesis onto the canonical Greek corpus.

finds.quote: Per the blind-reconstruction program (The Signature Without the Name, #1486), the channel families were registered before corpus contact: voice/tongue occlusion; fire in flesh; sight-failure; aural roar; sweat; tremor; pallor; death-adjacency; the jolt-lexeme. Diacritic-blind scan of the four canonical works (Perseus Greek: AJ 7,377 sections; Vita 430; Apion 617; BJ 4,002) returned NO section carrying three channels and no two-channel section with the collapse core. The null is retained as a finding about granularity: Josephus distributes the catalogue across sections and across persons, so the machine survives below co-occurrence resolution.
finds.points_to: channel families pre-registered per The Signature Without the Name, #1486
finds.note: Pre-registered scan reported as returning a null, retained as a finding.

finds.quote: The sharpest result. Josephus works from D, and at two joints he moves the scene CLOSER to fr. 31 than his source stands: he makes the voice-station explicit (ἀχανής, where D folds voice into the fall), and he tightens D's loose εἶδόν σε … καὶ ἐταράχθη into the poem's correlative ὡς γὰρ … εὐθύς. The signature intensifies downstream. Under the executable-transform model this is the predicted behavior of an attractor in transmission: second-order witnesses regress toward the pattern. Under any source-critical model it requires explanation; under this one it is the phenomenon.

finds.quote: Every entry point of the apparatus into canonical Josephus is Greek-Bible-layer material: Addition D (Alexandrian novella, Philo's city and near his era), the Genesis verb, the Elisha and Jeroboam narratives — plus the Herodian-erotic register of his Nicolaus material. The same Alexandrian channel that carried the machine into Philo's doctrine carried it into narrative, and Josephus, who names Sappho nowhere, transmits her syntax in a queen's confession and her terminus in a king's refusal of a death. The signature without the name, again — now with a syntactic bridge, a sequence invariant, and a lexical stitch, inside the corpus no one contests.
finds.note: Carrier thesis: the Alexandrian channel carried the pattern into Philo and Josephus.
